Given: The reader is near the top of a loaded history window, and the sixth question is not yet displayed.
When: Older messages load as the reader scrolls.
Then: The sixth question becomes visible and the previously visible anchor stays at the same screen position.
finding: Started from sixteen completed turns with question 6 unmounted. On a wheel event at scrollTop 4036, event …0038, “Turn 13, observation 3.” was at 448.75 px. When the older local page mounted and layout settled at 4680, the same text was still at 448.75 px. Question 6 was offscreen until another wheel reached 2336. With shorter earlier turns and a 1600 px browser height, a single wheel made question 6 visible, but question 9 moved from 1031 to 1019 px. A separate 51 px wheel moved the same control text from 84.25 to 135.25 px. The same delivery must show question 6 in the viewport while the pre-delivery event and text retain their screen coordinate. Recheck a change to native anchor compensation or page measurement.

Given: The reader is viewing the latest history window, with earlier groups not yet loaded.
When: They scroll near the top, away from it, and stop near the top again.
Then: The sixth question loads once and the original visible anchor stays at the same screen position; the fourth question remains absent.
finding: Drove near, away, then near again with trusted wheels. Question 6 mounted, unmounted, and mounted again. Question 4 stayed absent. The reference retained its position across each local layout. Repeating with the next wheel issued at the observed scroll event also produced two mounts. Look for a change to page retention or a continuous gesture with a single independently observed mount and the same pre-delivery text position.

Given: The reader is in history with a visible message anchored in the transcript.
When: Two completed replies arrive in succession.
Then: Both new replies become visible while the original anchor remains at the same screen position.
finding: Delivered two completed turns through separate catch-up responses. The locator showed 17 then 18 turns. At both arrivals the original text was at 263.25 px. The replies were mounted at 1507.75 and 1789.25 px, below the transcript bottom at 609 px. Both were readable after scrolling to the tail. A layout or presentation change must make both arriving replies visible in the viewport while preserving the history anchor.

Given: The reader is in history with a visible message anchored in the transcript.
When: A late-loaded image above the messages increases content height by 75 pixels.
Then: The anchored message remains at the same screen position.
finding: Scrolled the Markdown image into view to start an actual SVG request, then read a lower message while the receiver held the response. The image was above the anchor. After releasing the 240 × 75 SVG and awaiting browser decode, the thumbnail was still 198 × 178 px and the reference was still at 351.25 px. Exercise a supported late-loading media presentation that actually increases document height by 75 px.

Given: The reader reaches the tail, changes the live scroll offset to 275, and opens Automations at a narrow viewport.
When: A new reply containing a Mermaid diagram begins asynchronous image preparation, and the reader closes Automations before preparation finishes.
Then: The oldest message at the captured reading position remains at the same screen position while preparation is pending and after the diagram image is ready; the reader is not forced to the tail.
finding: At physical offset 275, delivered a diagram reply while Automations covered the transcript. The seventeenth marker arrived. The external image receiver had zero arrivals both before and after closing the panel. The same question returned at 296 px. Scrolling to the diagram then started the held image request. Revisit when rendering can start actual image preparation for the incoming reply while the transcript is hidden.

Given: The reader is in history on the primary conversation at a narrow viewport, and Automations covers the transcript.
When: They Alt-click a side conversation in the chat list, opening it alongside the primary conversation and dismissing Automations.
Then: The primary conversation remains at its route with the side conversation selected in the sidebar query, and the empty side conversation shows capability discovery. The original reading anchor is restored; subsequent image growth and incoming replies preserve its screen position without returning to the tail.
finding: At 930 px width the side conversation remained accessible under Automations. Alt-click opened the empty side conversation through the sidebar query, kept the primary route and exposed capability discovery. Primary text stayed at 385.25 px through reveal, the incoming reply and a real image decode. The reserved thumbnail stayed 198 × 178 px. Repeat behind a primary image whose rendered height genuinely grows. The 760 px layout did not expose the side-conversation link while covered.

Given: The reader reaches the tail, then changes the live scroll offset to 275 before opening Automations at a narrow viewport.
When: A new completed reply arrives while the transcript is hidden, and the reader closes Automations.
Then: The transcript restores to scroll offset 275 and the same message remains at the same screen position.
finding: Scrolled from the tail to physical offset 275 in a 760 px browser. Question 2, event …0004, was at 296 px. With Automations open the transcript height was zero and the seventeenth completed turn arrived. Closing returned the same text to 296 px at offset 275. A separate routed registration verifies offset and text position with the new reply already present before close. Complete. This GWT has no adjustment-count clause. The previously registered generic hidden-reply journey remains covered.

Given: The reader is in history at a narrow viewport, with a message anchored at the current reading position.
When: They open and close Automations, revealing the transcript.
Then: After the reveal, the anchored message returns to the same screen position with exactly one scroll adjustment.
finding: At 760 px the history text returned to 263.25 px and offset 4687. Browser animation frames observed 4687 → 0 while hidden and 0 → 4687 on reveal. The scrollTop, scroll, scrollTo and scrollBy observers registered zero application writes during reveal. Two same-frame control scrolls of +22 and −22 were both recorded. Browser visibility restoration and an explicit physical adjustment are distinguishable here. A receiver for compositor changes inside one frame, or an upstream statement defining the count, could resolve the frozen “exactly one.”

Given: The reader is in history with a message anchored before opening Automations.
When: A new completed reply arrives while the transcript is hidden, and the reader closes Automations.
Then: The original message remains at the same screen position after reveal, with one scroll adjustment.
finding: Repeated the narrow reveal after the same worker delivered turn 17 behind Automations. The marker was present before close. Offset 4687 and text position 263.25 px returned. Explicit scroll writes during reveal were zero, with one sampled transition and a two-write positive control. The single physical adjustment remains unproved. Preserve the separate completed-reply observation.

Given: The reader is in history in standalone PWA mode with a multiline draft in the composer.
When: They focus the composer through three keyboard-viewport shrink, pan, and restore cycles, then resize the layout viewport.
Then: The same message remains at the same reading position throughout, and the focused composer retains both draft lines through the keyboard cycles.
finding: Focused a two-line draft and ran three shrink/restore cycles in Chromium. Desktop layout resizing retained the reference. A PWA installation and launch succeeded, but the observed target reported standalone=false and no independent keyboard pan. Separately, a routed standalone VisualViewport fixture with distinct resize and pan inputs moved the text from 65 to −265 px. Use a standalone target that reports its display mode and a real nonzero visualViewport.offsetTop during keyboard use. Keep the existing tail regression separate.

Given: The reader is at the tail of a completed conversation with an empty composer.
When: They open Research from the Add menu, then close the capability tray.
Then: The transcript remains at the tail while the tray reduces its viewport height by 120 pixels and after it closes; the composer remains empty and the conversation route does not change.
finding: From a completed conversation at the tail, clicked Add, Research and Remove Research. Transcript heights were 561 → 201 → 561 px. Distance to the bottom stayed zero, the route stayed put, and the composer stayed empty. The measured reduction was 360 px. Revisit an actual 120 px tray layout or an upstream decision superseding that dimension.

Given: The reader is in history in a stopped conversation with an empty composer.
When: They open Research from the Add menu, then close the capability tray.
Then: The same message remains at the same reading position while the tray reduces its viewport height by 120 pixels and after it closes; the composer remains empty and the conversation route does not change.
finding: Delivered a terminal run.cancelled row and opened Research from history with an empty composer. The same text stayed at 249.25 px and scrollTop at 4701 through opening and removal. Heights were 561 → 201 → 561 px, with the route unchanged. The measured reduction was 360 px. A stopped conversation with a 120 px reduction, or a documented replacement for that contract, would settle this case.

Given: A restored recording contains 128 completed transcript segments.
When: The user chooses the recording when polishing is available.
Then: The composer receives all transcript text, grouped into 128 polish segments with one transcript per item; the audio is not retranscribed.
finding: Registered an independent 128-segment recovery trial at the ordinary 5000 ms suite limit. It supplied microphone PCM and received four transcriptions before timeout. It did not reach the restored editor or 128 polish groups in that registration. The previous long-run proof and short registered recovery control remain distinct. A representative saved 128-segment draft must be obtainable at a supported boundary within the normal suite run.

Given: A restored recording contains 129 completed transcript segments.
When: The user chooses the recording when polishing is available.
Then: The composer receives all transcript text, grouped into 65 polish segments with up to two transcripts per item; the audio is not retranscribed.
finding: The separate 129-segment trial supplied its own microphone capture. It reached four transcription responses before the ordinary 5000 ms limit, before recovery and the expected 65 polish items. The prior full-size supplemental recovery remains historical evidence. A regular registration must exercise the 129-to-65 boundary and detect any retranscription or lost final singleton.

Given: A finished voice draft contains no samples, with no prior samples segmented.
When: The next segment is requested.
Then: No segment is returned.
finding: Sent an empty microphone frame through the real recording page. Stop remained absent. A single positive sample enabled Stop. The WAV suite now registers that contrast. No finished zero-sample recording was produced through these controls. Find a supported device termination that completes an empty draft and permits a request for the next segment.

Given: A voice draft contains 73 seconds of samples after recovery, with a retained checkpoint at 60 seconds.
When: The next segment is requested before recording is finished.
Then: A non-final segment covers samples 58 through 73 seconds; the retained 60-second checkpoint is not resliced.
finding: Recorded exactly 60 seconds, navigated away after the fourth live WAV, and reopened the draft. The four live uploads ended at 15, 28, 41 and 54 seconds. Use recording was available without Resume. Its uploads covered 39–54 and 52–60 seconds. The continuous 73-second control has a different non-final 52–67 second window. A supported resume of a retained 60-second checkpoint must emit a non-final 58–73 second WAV. The initial fourth response raced navigation and was requested again on recovery.

Given: A user opens a Discord callback URL marked connected, but the account status says there is no verified connection.
When: The callback page loads.
Then: The user is taken to /settings/discord with status=connected and sees the Connect to Discord heading. No Connect action, Open Discord link, provider error detail, or completion request appears.
finding: Loaded the connected callback with an unverified member. Chromium showed Connect to Discord at /settings/discord?status=connected, enabled Connect, and exposed neither the provider detail nor Open Discord. The independent HTTP receiver observed only a status GET between navigation and departure. It recorded a rejected completion POST sent afterwards as a positive control. Upstream explicitly expects Connect for this indicator and unverified status. Closed against the sourced correction. The frozen “no Connect” clause receives no original-GWT acceptance.

Given: Discord is disconnected, and the user leaves Works for Chat while Discord status refresh is pending.
When: The user returns to Works before the refresh completes.
Then: The Discord card continues to show its description and an enabled Connect button; after refresh it shows Connected.
finding: Started disconnected, held the change-triggered status request, left for Chat and returned before release. The description remained with no buttons. Delivery exposed Connected and enabled More options. In a separate control where refresh started only on return, the card retained enabled Connect until delivery. Both chronologies have a regular registration. The upstream cache promise covers refresh starting on return. A change or a product ruling on refresh already pending before departure could close the original.

Given: Discord is connected, and the user leaves Works for Chat while Discord status refresh is pending.
When: The user returns to Works before the refresh completes.
Then: The Discord card continues to show its description and Connected status; after refresh it still shows Connected.
finding: Started connected, held refresh before leaving Works and returned while pending. The card showed its description without Connected or actions. The response restored Connected and enabled More options. Starting refresh only on return preserved the cached Connected state. Both initial states and both chronologies were exercised. Look for a decision or implementation that preserves a connected card across departure with a status request already pending.

Given: Discord initially shows Connected, then a status refresh is denied with a 403 error.
When: The user returns to Works after leaving for Chat, once status access is available again.
Then: During the error, the card shows “Discord access denied” and its description, with no buttons or stale Connected status. On returning, it shows Connected again.
finding: A connected member received HTTP 403 on status refresh. The global notice said “Discord access denied”. The Discord card kept its description with zero actions and no stale Connected status. After leaving for Chat and returning with access restored, Connected and More options returned. The upstream change asserts the notice at page scope and the description and actions at card scope. Closed against the sourced correction to the error surface. No first acceptance of the frozen card-scoped claim.
